title: Anthropic prices record IPO at $83 a share, raising about $81.3 billion and topping SpaceX
verification: TechCrunch (Nov 18): priced at $83, above $70-$78 range; 980 million shares, up from 825 million; $81.3 billion in proceeds, surpassing SpaceX's $75 billion record, largest IPO in history by proceeds; about $1.5 trillion fully diluted; Nasdaq ticker ANT, trading Thursday; Spark Capital led the $450 million Series C in 2023 at a $4.5 billion valuation; Amazon owns nearly 15%, Google almost 14%. Fortune (Nov 18): same price, range, share count, $1.5 trillion; second most valuable IPO behind SpaceX's $1.77 trillion in June; revenue $33.2 billion for the nine months to September 30 vs $2.5 billion a year earlier; $104 billion net loss, mostly from accounting for convertible notes; seven cofounders about five years ago; Dario Amodei left OpenAI at end of 2020. NPR and CNBC headlines confirm the $81.3 billion record (NPR: company itself about $79.4 billion, rest sold by existing holders). 1.5T / 4.5B = 333x. Claim check: 'biggest IPO' limited to money raised.

slides.headline: The biggest IPO in history isn't SpaceX's anymore.

image.credit: Photo: Nasdaq MarketSite, Times Square. ajay_suresh / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0

slides.text: It's Anthropic, the company behind the AI assistant Claude. On November 18 it priced its shares at $83 and raised about $81.3 billion. SpaceX's record from June: $75 billion.

image.credit: Photo: inside Anthropic's San Francisco office, 2024. Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (UK) / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0

slides.text: Demand was so strong that Anthropic set the price above its planned $70 to $78. It also sold 980 million shares instead of the 825 million it first offered.
CEO Dario Amodei left OpenAI at the end of 2020 and started Anthropic with six other cofounders. At $83 a share, it is now valued at about $1.5 trillion.

image.credit: Photo: Dario Amodei in 2023. TechCrunch / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0

slides.text: Revenue in the first nine months of 2026: $33.2 billion, up from $2.5 billion a year earlier. Same nine months: a $104 billion net loss, mostly from how it accounts for certain notes.

image.credit: Photo: Anthropic cofounder Jack Clark. Mvolz / Wikimedia Commons, CC0

slides.text: In 2023, investors valued the whole company at $4.5 billion. The IPO price puts it more than 300 times higher. Shares trade on Nasdaq as ANT.

caption:
Three years ago, you could have bought into Anthropic at a $4.5 billion valuation.

On November 18, its IPO priced at $83 a share, above the $70 to $78 range it had planned. It sold 980 million shares instead of 825 million and raised about $81.3 billion. That beats the $75 billion SpaceX raised in June, making it the largest IPO ever by money raised.

By total value, SpaceX still leads: it went public at about $1.77 trillion. Anthropic comes in at about $1.5 trillion.

The numbers behind the rush: $33.2 billion in revenue in the first nine months of 2026, up from $2.5 billion a year before. The same period shows a $104 billion net loss, which the company says comes mostly from how it accounts for convertible notes.

Amazon owns nearly 15% of the company and Google almost 14%. Seven partners, including Google and Nvidia, also agreed to buy $26 billion of non-voting stock at the IPO price.

OpenAI, its main rival, has not set a date for its own IPO.

Source: TechCrunch, Fortune, CNBC, NPR
